ModMetaData.name: Moving Dunes
ModMetaData.author: mandrake
ModMetaData.description:
Sand that actually moves.
Odyssey already gives a map a per-cell sand depth, a renderer, path penalties, a clear-sand job and a sandstorm that drops sand out of the sky. What it never does is move the sand afterwards — it lands where it fell and evaporates within days. This mod adds the missing half.
On a dune-field biome the map gets a prevailing wind direction of its own, which shifts every few days. Sand erodes off exposed crests and hops downwind in slabs, banking wherever it finds shelter — behind a wall, at the lip of a roof, or in any hollow lower than the ground it came from. Dug pits and cleared lanes refill from that same rule, so a maintained trench upwind becomes a sand moat you keep re-digging. A wall line across the prevailing wind becomes a real windbreak, and where your base faces becomes a layout decision.
The map is treated as a window onto an endless desert rather than a loop: sand blowing off the downwind edge is gone for good, and fresh sand arrives along the upwind edge at a rate the material sets. A storm brings more of it.
Loose gear left out in the desert gets swallowed. A buried stack stops deteriorating and waits; when the wind turns and the drift over it erodes away, it comes back out. Anything in a stockpile or inside your home area is left alone. Plants under deep drift choke and die, so an advancing front leaves a dead strip behind it.
Every number is data. A dune material def carries the colour, the slab size, hop distance, wind threshold, supply rate, storm multipliers, burial and reveal depths and the plant-choke timing, so a desert can drift pale sand while an ash field drifts grey on the same machinery. Biomes opt in one at a time; vanilla Desert and Extreme Desert are bound here, and other mods bind their own.
Other mods can bury things directly (BuryThingsAt) so wrecks and dig sites can start the game already under the sand.
Requires Odyssey: the sand grid is Odyssey's, and without it this mod is inert rather than broken.
